title: Shopify Upgrades Checkout Blocks to Polaris Web Components, Cutting Bundle Sizes up to 85%
gist: Shopify rebuilt five Checkout Blocks UI extensions (rendering on ~1/3 of customized checkouts) from React/Remote UI to Preact + Polaris web components, cutting transferred bundle sizes 40-85% and load time ~8% at median; the move to API 2026-01 is mandatory from Oct 1, 2026, and developer sentiment has turned mixed.

insights.claim: Shopify's Checkout Blocks extensions saw transferred bundle sizes fall 40-85% after moving to Preact and Polaris web components, with the payment-icons extension shrinking 84.4%.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Quantifies the performance dividend from abandoning heavy React runtimes in latency-critical commerce surfaces.
insights.quote: Transferred bundle sizes fell between 40 percent and 85 percent across the extension family, with the payment-icons extension shrinking by 84.4 percent.

insights.claim: Extension Load Time for Shopify's Checkout Blocks dropped around 8% at the median and 7% at p90, weighted by checkout volume.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Modest load-time gains on checkout can still matter for conversion at Shopify's scale.

insights.claim: A hard 64KB gzip per-extension budget enforced by the 2026-01 remote-dom CLI drove much of the size reduction, versus prior bundles of ~100-112KB gzipped.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Platform-imposed budgets, not voluntary optimization, are what force ecosystem-wide performance improvements.
insights.quote: Much of that was driven by a hard 64KB gzip budget that the 2026-01 remote-dom CLI enforces per extension

insights.claim: Switching from React to Preact removed react-reconciler and saved roughly 89KB, while an in-house 13KB Liquid parser ('droplet') replaced the ~73KB liquidjs, validated on a 42,000-line parity corpus of real merchant configs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Signals large platforms will replace third-party OSS dependencies with lean in-house versions when size budgets bind.
insights.locator: Switching from React to Preact removed

insights.claim: From October 1, 2026, Shopify will block app deployments that include checkout extension versions earlier than API 2026-01, making the web-components migration mandatory.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Creates a hard deadline and migration workload for the Shopify app developer ecosystem.
insights.quote: The change is not optional: from October 1, 2026, app deployments will be blocked if they include extension versions earlier than 2026-01.
insights.locator: Shopify has detailed how it rebuilt

insights.claim: Shopify is shifting its entire UI extension surface onto framework-agnostic s-* custom elements loaded from its CDN, reducing dependence on React as the extension framework.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Points to a broader industry drift from framework-specific component libraries toward web standards, weakening React lock-in on platforms.
insights.locator: For developers starting their own migration

insights.claim: Early reception of Shopify's Preact/web-components move in late 2025 was largely positive, with Gadget calling it 'a great update' and Hacker News users welcoming components shipped without the Shadow DOM.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Initial developer goodwill supports adoption, but is not the full picture.

insights.claim: Developers have complained that Shopify ships an unversioned CDN script that cannot be pinned, calling it 'a nightmare for stability', and that the new components are 'incomplete', lacking e.g. Polaris React's Index Table.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Platform-controlled unversioned dependencies create stability risk for merchants' apps and friction for the app ecosystem.

insights.claim: Some developers caution that web components are 'not a panacea' and will not replace framework component systems.
insights.speaker: Daniel Curtis
insights.so_what: Tempers the thesis that web components will displace React-style frameworks broadly.
